findings.title: Accidental submodule/gitlink `sentry-repo` committed at PR base commit
findings.body: The PR adds a file `sentry-repo` whose only content is `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` (the PR base SHA), with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry in the change. This is a gitlink to a nested repository checkout, almost certainly committed by accident. Checking it in makes the tree contain a broken/uninitialized submodule reference that can confuse CI, `git submodule` tooling, and clean checkouts. It is unrelated to the feature and should be removed before merge.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses outer `dataset`/`request.GET` instead of the actual `scoped_dataset`/`query`
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` computes `should_upsample` with `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` using the closure variable `dataset` (the originally requested dataset from `get_dataset`) and re-reading `request.GET['query']`. But the actual query built below uses the first parameter `scoped_dataset` and the `query` argument, which in the dashboard discover-split path (lines ~345-452) differ: `_get_event_stats` is called with `discover` and query strings like `(<query>) AND !event.type:transaction` or `(<query>) AND event.type:transaction`. In those calls the eligibility decision is evaluated against the wrong dataset and the wrong query string, so upsampling is either silently skipped for an error sub-query or applied to a transaction sub-query (where `sample_weight` is null), yielding wrong counts. The eligibility check should receive `scoped_dataset` and the actual `query` being executed.

findings.title: `_is_error_focused_query` substring match matches negated and mixed queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the raw query string contains the substring `event.type:error`, using `'event.type:error' in query`. That is true for negated filters such as `!event.type:error` (which selects transactions) and for mixed clauses such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. In those cases upsampling is enabled and `count()` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()` even though the query includes/excludes transactions, so `sum(sample_weight)` runs over events that have no sample weight and the reported count is wrong. The check needs to parse the filter rather than do a substring search (or at least exclude negated occurrences).

findings.title: `errors` dataset enables `upsampled_count` but function is only registered in DiscoverDataset
findings.body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True for `sentry.snuba.errors`, so `count()` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()` for `dataset=errors` requests. However the new `upsampled_count` SnQL function is only added to `DiscoverDataset.function_converter` (src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py). If `ErrorsQueryBuilder`/the errors dataset resolves functions through a different converter that does not know `upsampled_count`, every errors-dataset stats request for an allowlisted org will fail with an unknown-function error at query time. Verify the errors dataset shares DiscoverDataset's function converter, or register `upsampled_count` there as well.

findings.title: `sum(sample_weight)` silently drops events with NULL sample_weight
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is defined as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. ClickHouse `sum` ignores NULL inputs, so any event whose `sample_weight` is NULL is excluded from the count. The helper claims the schema guarantees `sample_weight` for all events (error_upsampling.py:85), but the only code populating it in this PR is gated on `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` (factories.py), i.e. only explicitly sampled events appear to have a weight. Events in an allowlisted project that were ingested without a client sample rate would have NULL `sample_weight` and vanish from the upsampled count, undercounting. Confirm the ingest pipeline writes a default weight of 1 for unsampled events, or use `sum(coalesce(sample_weight, 1))`.

findings.title: Cache lookup and option read run for every stats request regardless of dataset
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` builds the cache key and performs `cache.get` before checking whether the dataset is even relevant, and then still calls `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` on a cache hit. `organization_events_stats` is a high-volume endpoint used for transactions/spans/logs, where the result is always discarded, so this adds a cache round-trip (and, on miss, an option read plus `cache.set`) to requests that can never use upsampling. Evaluate `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)` first and only do the allowlist cache lookup when it is True.

findings.title: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called; stale eligibility after allowlist changes
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` documents that it must be called when the allowlist configuration changes, but nothing in this PR calls or wires it up. Changing `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` therefore leaves stale eligibility cached for up to 60s per org/project-set, so a newly allowlisted (or de-allowlisted) project keeps the old behavior until the TTL expires. Also note the contradictory documentation: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` says it always reads the allowlist fresh, while its caller caches the result for 60s. Either wire invalidation into the option-update path or remove the function and correct the docstrings.

findings.title: Empty-allowlist branch is not actually tested
findings.body: Under the comment 'Test when no projects are allowlisted' the test sets `mock_options.get.return_value = []` but then calls `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled([], self.organization)` with an empty project list. That returns False via the earlier `if not project_ids` guard, never reaching the `if not allowlist: return False` branch. The intended case (non-empty project ids with an empty allowlist) is therefore untested; pass `self.project_ids` instead of `[]` to exercise it.
